definition: Monism is the view that the universe is the expression or operation of one underlying principle. In historical philosophical and psychological discussion, it has been contrasted with dualism and pluralism, and has also been used more narrowly for positions that treat mind and body as different aspects or manifestations of a single basis rather than two separate interacting substances.
